newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says no intention of changing Italy ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says no intention of changing Italy ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Friday it had no intention of changing either the long-term local currency or the long-term foreign currency ratings of the Republic of Italy's sovereign debt.
It said the Republic of Italy was not on RatingWatch.

"IBCA confirms its AA minus long-term foreign currency rating, applied to senior and unsecured foreign currency debt obligations of the Republic, its rating of A1 plus for short-term foreign currency issues and the long-term local currency rating of AAA," IBCA said in a statement.
Rumors swirled through Italian financial markets earlier that a credit rating agency might downgrade Italian debt.
The Italian Treasury said that Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's had denied any plans to downgrade Italy's ratings.
